title: Almond Marzipan Fruits
summary: Cooked almond marzipan coloured and hand-shaped into small peaches, pears, lemons and strawberries.
equipment: heatproof work surface or silicone mat

ingredients.item: icing sugar, plus extra for dusting
gel food colouring in red, orange, yellow and green, a little of each

steps.title: Get ready
steps.text: Dust a heatproof work surface with icing sugar and half-fill a large bowl with cold water, big enough to stand the saucepan in.

steps.title: Boil the syrup
steps.text: Put the sugar, cream of tartar and water in the saucepan over medium-high heat and stir until the sugar dissolves. Then boil without stirring until it reads 116 °C.

steps.title: Cool the syrup
steps.text: Stand the pan in the cold water and stir for 2-3 min, until the syrup turns cloudy and creamy.

steps.title: Cook the paste
steps.text: Stir in the almond flour and egg white. Put the pan back over low heat and stir constantly until the paste is thick, smooth and reads at least 72 °C.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Tip it onto the sugared surface. When cool enough to handle, knead in the icing sugar until smooth and pliable like modelling clay.

steps.title: Colour
steps.text: Divide the marzipan into four and wrap three portions. Knead a little colouring into each portion in turn: pale orange for peaches, yellow-green for pears, yellow for lemons and red for strawberries.

steps.title: Shape the fruits
steps.text: Roll 20 g balls. Mark a seam down each peach and brush on a red blush, taper the pears at one end, pinch the lemons at both ends and roll them over the fine grater for texture, and shape the strawberries into cones dotted all over with a cocktail stick.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Push a clove into the peaches and pears as a stem, add small green marzipan leaves to the strawberries and leave uncovered for 2 h to firm up.

tips: The most common mistake is adding too much colour at once; start with a dot of gel on a cocktail stick and build up.
Keep the portions you are not shaping wrapped, as marzipan dries and cracks quickly.
Remove the clove stems before eating.
safety: Egg safety: the egg white is cooked to at least 72 °C; for extra safety use pasteurised egg white.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep the fruits covered at room temperature for up to 1 week; plain wrapped marzipan keeps in the fridge for up to 2 months.
